week.title: The Room Changes

opening_illustration.alt_text: Grete and Mrs. Samsa remove furniture from Gregor's bedroom while Gregor watches from the darker side of the room. The room is beginning to look empty.

part_illustrations.alt_text: Grete and Mrs. Samsa prepare to remove furniture while Gregor watches from the darker side of the bedroom.
Gregor looks at his desk, chair and framed picture and remembers his human life.
Gregor covers the framed picture on the wall while Grete and Mrs. Samsa stand near the doorway.
Mrs. Samsa becomes frightened and weak while Grete supports her and Gregor stays back.
Mr. Samsa throws apples while Gregor tries to retreat toward his bedroom.
Gregor lies weak in the nearly empty bedroom after the conflict, surrounded by very few reminders of his old life.

before_you_read: Do objects in your room have special memories for you?
Can a room show something about a person's life?
How do you feel when someone changes your things without asking?
story: Gregor spends more time climbing the walls.
His new body can move easily on them.
Sometimes he climbs to the ceiling.
She thinks Gregor needs more space.
One day, she talks to her mother.
“We can remove some furniture,” Grete says.
His picture is still on the wall.
“But this is Gregor's room,” she says.
She believes the furniture is now a problem.
Gregor listens to them from inside the room.
At first, he understands Grete's idea.
He can climb better without the furniture.
He remembers his human body sitting in it.
These things are not only furniture.
They are part of his old life.
If everything leaves the room, what remains?
They begin to move the furniture.
The women move the heavy desk.
He cannot say: “Please leave my things here.”
He cannot explain that the furniture is important.
Then he sees the picture on the wall.
He does not want to lose it.
Mrs. Samsa returns to the room.
Gregor does not want to hurt her.
He does not want to frighten her.
But he cannot change what he is.
He is wearing his work uniform.
He looks stronger and more serious.
Grete tells him that something happened.
Mr. Samsa sees Gregor outside his normal hiding place.
Gregor tries to return to his room.
But his father moves toward him.
He cannot say: “I am not attacking anyone.”
He cannot say: “I only want my things.”
Mr. Samsa picks up apples from a bowl.
She asks her husband to stop.
Gregor finally returns to his room.
Gregor looks at what is left.
But now the empty space feels strange.
The room gives him more freedom to move.
But it also has less of Gregor Samsa inside it.

visual_reflection.title: Gregor Protects the Picture
visual_reflection.alt_text: Gregor is on the wall of his bedroom, covering a framed picture with his transformed body. Some furniture has already been moved. Grete and Mrs. Samsa stand near the doorway.
questions: What is different about the room?
Why is the picture important to Gregor?

items: Gregor wants to ______ something from his old life.
He covers the ______ on the wall.

reading_comprehension.question: Why does Grete want to remove the furniture?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because she thinks Gregor needs more space to move and climb.

reading_comprehension.question: Why is Mrs. Samsa not sure about the idea?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because the room and furniture are connected to Gregor's human life.

reading_comprehension.question: What does Gregor remember when he looks at his desk and chair?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: He remembers studying, working and using them as a human.

reading_comprehension.question: Why does Gregor become anxious?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because the furniture is being removed and he feels he is losing part of his old life.

reading_comprehension.question: What object does Gregor try to protect?
What happens when Mrs. Samsa sees Gregor?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: She becomes very frightened and weak.

reading_comprehension.question: How has Mr. Samsa changed?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: He works again, wears a uniform and appears stronger and more authoritative.

reading_comprehension.question: Why does Mr. Samsa become angry?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: He believes Gregor has caused a dangerous problem.

reading_comprehension.question: Why does the empty room make Gregor sad?
reading_comprehension.suggested_answer: Because it contains less of his old human life and identity.

true_false.statement: Grete wants Gregor to have more space.
Mrs. Samsa immediately wants to remove everything.
Gregor does not care about his old furniture.
Gregor protects a picture on the wall.
Mr. Samsa comes home wearing a work uniform.
Gregor becomes weaker after the conflict.

reflection.title: Think About the Story
reflection.prompt: Can something help Gregor's new body but hurt Gregor emotionally?

items: Gregor ______ explain his feelings to his family.
Mrs. Samsa ______ see Gregor without becoming frightened.
Gregor cannot ______ at his old job.

speaking_mission.title: Keep It or Remove It?
speaking_mission.challenge: What is more important: space or memory?

writing_mission.title: Gregor's Room
writing_mission.instruction: Write about what should stay in Gregor's room and explain why.

questions: Is Gregor protecting an expensive object?
Or is he protecting a memory?

kafkas_question.prompt: If Gregor loses the things from his human life, does he lose part of his identity too?

deeper_question.prompt: Can a good intention still hurt someone?

father_and_son.prompt: How is the relationship between Gregor and his father changing?

prediction.context: Gregor is hurt. He is weaker. The family needs money. Everyone is changing.
prediction.question: What do you think happens next?

learning_outcomes: Understand why the furniture is important.
Understand the changing relationship between Gregor and his father.
See how the whole Samsa family is changing.

next_week.teaser: Time passes. Gregor becomes weaker. His room becomes less important. His family continues living. And one night, Gregor hears something beautiful: Grete's violin.
